items.title: Avoiding Bias and Ensuring Inclusivity in AI Design

source_refs.note: Unnumbered topic Avoiding Bias and Ensuring Inclusivity in AI Design under 8.2 as printed (PDF 114, printed 110).

blocks.text: AI systems often learn from large datasets, which may contain hidden biases. For example, if a hiring system is trained mostly on past records where men were selected more often than women, the AI may unfairly prefer male candidates. Similarly, if a face recognition system is trained mainly on images of one age group, skin tone, or region, it may perform poorly for people from other groups. Developers must carefully review and adjust these datasets to avoid unfair treatment of individuals or groups. Inclusivity in AI design means considering diverse perspectives and ensuring that technology serves all people equally, regardless of gender, ethnicity, or background.
